A simulation-based likelihood is computed from a finite number of simulated
trials, so it is noisy, and the optimizer searches a five-dimensional space
with that noisy function. A returned estimate is therefore not, by itself,
evidence of a reliable fit. This vignette explains what can go wrong, how
funresMech detects it and what to do.

## What can go wrong

| Problem | Why it happens |
|---|---|
| Monte Carlo noise | Each evaluation of the likelihood uses a finite number of simulated trials (`n_sim`). Two evaluations at the same parameters give slightly different values. |
| Optimizer stopped early | The optimizer has a limited number of generations (`itermax`) and population size (`NP`). |
| Optimizer exploited the noise | The minimum found during the search is biased downward because it is the smallest of many noisy values. funresMech therefore uses the mean of independent re-evaluations at each optimum. |
| Estimate on a search bound | The optimum may lie outside the default search range. Bounds are widened automatically, but the check remains. |
| Weak identification | With very irregular search times (small `k`), several combinations of `a`, `z` and `k` fit almost equally well and the interval of `z` can stay open. |
| Observed outcomes never simulated | If no simulated trial produces an observed count, its probability is set to a tiny floor that adds 708 units to the NLL. More simulations usually resolve it. |

## The checks

`reliability(fit)` returns one row per check, with a status (`ok`,
`warning` or `fail`), the value that was checked and the recommended action.
`verify_fit(fit)` adds the checks that need extra optimizations.

| Check | Warning or failure when | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Observed outcomes produced by the simulation | An observed count was never simulated at the optimum (fail) or at other profile points (warning). | Increase `n_sim`; check atypical trials; check that the model can produce these outcomes. |
| Estimates away from search bounds | An estimate ends on a bound. | Widen the bounds with `funres_control(bounds = ...)`. |
| Monte Carlo noise of the NLL | The standard error of the NLL at the optimum exceeds 0.25. | Increase `n_sim`. |
| Optimizer value versus re-evaluated NLL | The re-evaluated NLL exceeds the optimizer's value by more than 2 units. | Increase `n_sim`. |
| Optimizer settled before the end of the run | The NLL improved by more than 1 unit in the last quarter of the run. | Increase `itermax` (and `NP`). |
| Profile of z regular | The profile has extra local minima beyond Monte Carlo noise. | Increase `itermax`, `NP` and `n_sim` and refit. |
| Interval of z closed | A limit of the interval is open. | Extend the grid of `z`; an open limit after extension means that the data do not bound `z` on that side. |
| Search dispersion k not extreme | `k` < 0.1. | Check the screening for atypical trials; consider fixing `k` and comparing by AIC. |
| Independent runs agree (NLL) | The NLL of independent runs differs by more than 0.5 (warning) or 1.92 (fail). | Increase `itermax`, `NP` and `n_sim`. |
| Independent runs agree (a, h) | `a` or `h` differ by more than 25% between runs. | More effort; interpret `a` and `h` with caution. |
| More effort does not improve the optimum | Twice the effort improves the NLL by more than 1 unit. | Refit the whole profile with more simulations and generations (`n_sim`, `itermax`). |
| Wider bounds do not improve the optimum | Bounds ten times wider improve the NLL by more than 1 unit. | Refit with wider bounds. |

## A recommended workflow

```{r workflow}
library(funresMech)
future::plan(future::multisession)

screen_outliers(d, T = 24)                           # 1. atypical trials

set.seed(1)
fit <- fit_funres(d, T = 24,                          # 2. first look
                  control = funres_control(n_sim = 2000, itermax = 50, n_reeval = 3))
reliability(fit)

set.seed(2)
fit <- fit_funres(d, T = 24,                          # 3. fit to report
                  control = funres_control())
fit <- verify_fit(fit)                                # 4. verification
reliability(fit)                                      # 5. no check may fail
```

If a check fails, follow its action and refit. If the interval of `z`
remains open after the grid was extended, report it as open: the data do not
bound `z` on that side.

## How well does the method work?

The estimation procedure was evaluated with simulated data whose parameters
were known (three values of `z`, three levels of `k`, designs with 5, 8 and 13
host densities):

* The estimates of `z` and `h` were unbiased. `k` tended to be overestimated,
  so it should not be over-interpreted.
* The 95% interval of `z` contained the true value in 91% of 288 fits (95%
  confidence interval 87% to 94%). The interval is thus slightly narrower
  than nominal. Coverage was lowest with highly variable search times
  (`k` = 0.2) and reached 94% with 13 host densities. Numerical causes
  (optimization, Monte Carlo noise, grid spacing, interpolation) were ruled
  out; the remaining undercoverage is a property of the likelihood-ratio
  interval with small samples.
* When the true response was type II, the interval excluded `z` = 1 in 4% to
  8% of the fits. When `z` was 1.75 or 2.75, it excluded `z` = 1 in 83% to
  100% of the fits.
* With the default settings (`n_sim = 5000`, `itermax = 100`), the checks gave
  false alarms in at most 6% of the fits. With cheaper settings
  (`n_sim = 2000`, `itermax = 50`), about half of the fits received warnings
  about noise or convergence, as intended.
* The cheaper settings gave the same coverage as the defaults but less
  reliable optima, so report fits made with at least the default effort and
  checked with `verify_fit()`.

## Recommendations for experimental design

* Use at least 8 host densities, spread over the whole range from very low to
  saturating densities, with replicates at every density.
* Low densities are informative about `z`, because the shape of the response
  at low densities distinguishes type II from type III.
* Keep the original data of every trial. Means per density cannot be
  analyzed with this method.

## What to report

* The package version, the model (distributions, process, fixed
  parameters), the settings of `funres_control()`, and the random seed.
* The estimates with the 95% interval of `z`, stating whether a limit is
  open.
* The result of `reliability()` after `verify_fit()`.
* The result of the screening for atypical trials and, if any trial was
  flagged, the analysis with and without it.

The application exports all of these, including an R script that repeats the
analysis.
